evals.query: Set up a Kora 2.0 Java Cassandra repository for a User entity (String id, name, email, createdAt) with findById, findAll, insert and deleteById.
expected_behavior: Adds implementation "io.koraframework:database-cassandra" versioned through the io.koraframework:kora-bom platform, plus annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors"
Uses koraVersion 2.0.0.RC2 from plain mavenCentral(), not 2.0.0-SNAPSHOT and not the kora-parent BOM
Adds CassandraDatabaseModule (io.koraframework.database.cassandra) to the @KoraApp interface
Declares an interface annotated @Repository (io.koraframework.database.common.annotation.Repository) that extends CassandraRepository
Annotates the DAO record with @EntityCassandra imported from io.koraframework.database.cassandra.annotation, not from io.koraframework.database.cassandra
Writes CQL in @Query with :id style named parameters and marks the single-row lookup @Nullable using org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable
Does not import ru.tinkoff.kora.* anywhere, and does not declare com.datastax.oss:java-driver-core as a dependency
Does not invent an @Id requirement — @Id and @Table matter only to SQL macros in Cassandra

evals.query: My Kora Cassandra module fails to resolve com.datastax.oss:java-driver-core:4.17.0 after upgrading to Kora 2.0. My mappers import com.datastax.oss.driver.api.core.cql.Row — do I have to rewrite those imports too?
expected_behavior: Explains that the driver moved Maven coordinates to org.apache.cassandra:java-driver-core (4.19.3 in Kora 2.0), so the com.datastax.oss groupId no longer resolves
States clearly that the Java package names did NOT change — com.datastax.oss.driver.api.* imports stay exactly as they are
Recommends removing the explicit driver dependency entirely and letting io.koraframework:database-cassandra bring it transitively
Does not tell the user to rewrite imports to an org.apache.cassandra.* package, which does not exist
Does not suggest pinning the driver version by hand when the kora-bom platform is in use

evals.query: Port this Kora 1.x Kotlin Cassandra repository to 2.0: `@Repository interface UserRepository : CassandraRepository { @Query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = :id") suspend fun findById(id: String): User?; @Query("SELECT * FROM users") fun findAllFlow(): Flow<User> }`
expected_behavior: Removes suspend and returns User? from a plain fun
Replaces Flow<User> with List<User>, noting result size should be bounded with CQL LIMIT or basic.request.pageSize
Explains that KSP rejects suspend repository methods outright with 'Suspend methods are not supported by the repository generator.'
States that Kotlin Cassandra repositories are synchronous only and run on virtual threads — no suspend, no Flow, no Mono/Flux
Points at java.util.concurrent.StructuredTaskScope (or virtual-thread executors) for parallel fan-out instead of coroutines
Does not add kotlinx-coroutines-core or io.projectreactor:reactor-core for the repository
Does not claim a CompletableFuture return type is the Kotlin workaround — the async path exists only in the Java generator

evals.query: I want non-blocking Cassandra access from my Kora 2.0 Java service. Show me what is actually supported.
expected_behavior: Provides methods returning CompletableFuture<T> and CompletionStage<T>, including CompletionStage<Void> for writes and CompletionStage<List<T>> for lists
Keeps the @Query CQL identical to the synchronous version, changing only the return type
Explains that Cassandra is the exception to Kora 2.0's synchronous-only contracts because the generator uses the driver's prepareAsync/executeAsync
States that Mono/Flux and CassandraReactiveResultSetMapper were removed and that reactor-core must not be added
Notes that the equivalent does not exist in Kotlin
Mentions CassandraAsyncResultSetMapper only as the async result contract, wired automatically for entity results
Does not block a future with .get()/.join() inside the repository or inside a stage callback

evals.query: My Kora 1.x code calls repository.getCassandraConnectionFactory().currentSession() to run a dynamic CQL query. It does not compile on Kora 2.0. Also, how do I wrap two writes in a transaction there?
expected_behavior: Replaces getCassandraConnectionFactory() with executor(), returning io.koraframework.database.cassandra.CassandraExecutor
Shows CassandraExecutor members actually available: currentSession(), telemetry(), query(...), queryOne(...), queryOptional(...), queryList(...)
Introduces CassandraQuery.named()/template() with bind/bindIf/cqlIf/bindIn for the dynamic query, rather than string-concatenating user values into CQL
States plainly that Cassandra has no transactions and CassandraExecutor has no inTx — unlike JdbcExecutor
Offers lightweight transactions (IF / IF NOT EXISTS, single partition, boolean [applied]) as the nearest real mechanism, and does not present them as multi-statement transactions
Does not invent a CassandraConnectionFactory type or a transaction API

evals.query: I converted this Java Cassandra mapper to Kotlin and now KSP says "'apply' overrides nothing": `class StatusParameterMapper : CassandraParameterColumnMapper<Status> { override fun apply(stmt: SettableByName<*>, index: Int, value: Status) { stmt.setInt(index, value.code) } }`
expected_behavior: Identifies the cause as nullability: the contract declares void apply(SettableByName<?> stmt, int index, @Nullable T value), so the Kotlin override must take value: Status?
Provides the fixed signature with value: Status? and a null branch calling stmt.setToNull(index)
Explains that the contracts are @NullMarked so Kotlin overrides must match declared nullability exactly, and that the compiler error never mentions nullability
Notes the asymmetry — the Java version compiles either way, so mechanically ported mappers fail only on the Kotlin side
Notes that return types may still be narrowed to non-null, e.g. CassandraRowMapper.apply(row: Row): T
Does not suggest @field:Nullable or any JSpecify annotation in Kotlin

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 build fails with "No component found for dependency: io.koraframework.database.cassandra.mapper.result.CassandraRowMapper<Event>". The mapper class takes an ObjectMapper in its constructor and is referenced with @Mapping on the repository method.
expected_behavior: Explains that the generated repository constructs a mapper itself only when it is final (Java) or non-open (Kotlin) with a no-arg constructor and an untagged @Mapping

Concludes that a mapper with constructor dependencies becomes a constructor parameter of the generated repository and must therefore be annotated @Component (io.koraframework.common.annotation.Component)
Warns that declaring two components for the same mapper type produces 'Multiple components match dependency:' instead
Mentions that @EntityCassandra on the row type is the alternative when a plain entity mapper is all that is needed
Notes that Kora's own scalar mappers in CassandraMapperModule are @DefaultComponent, so a user @Component for the same type replaces them without conflict
Does not advise adding @Component blindly to every mapper regardless of its constructor

evals.query: Configure the Cassandra connection for my Kora 2.0 service in HOCON: contact points, datacenter, keyspace, credentials from environment variables, a 5 second request timeout, and I want to see the query logs and db metrics.
expected_behavior: Uses the cassandra top-level section — not db, not jdbc, and not a renamed 2.0 section
Places contactPoints, dc and sessionKeyspace under cassandra.basic, and timeout under cassandra.basic.request
Places credentials under cassandra.auth.login and cassandra.auth.password with ${CASSANDRA_USER} style substitutions
Explicitly sets cassandra.telemetry.logging.enabled = true and cassandra.telemetry.metrics.enabled = true, stating that both default to false in Kora 2.0
Does not invent keys such as healthCheck, retryPolicy, basic.consistency, requestTimeout, cassandra.keyspace or root-level username/password
Does not claim the section was renamed the way JDBC's db became jdbc

evals.query: Give me the exact import list for a Kora 2.0 Cassandra repository that uses @Repository, @Query, @Batch, @EntityCassandra, @UDT, @CassandraProfile, @Table, @Column and @Id.
expected_behavior: Puts @Repository, @Query, @Batch, @Table, @Column, @Id (and @Embedded) in io.koraframework.database.common.annotation
Puts @EntityCassandra, @UDT and @CassandraProfile in io.koraframework.database.cassandra.annotation
Puts CassandraRepository and CassandraExecutor in io.koraframework.database.cassandra
Does not place @EntityCassandra or @UDT directly in io.koraframework.database.cassandra without the .annotation sub-package
Does not use ru.tinkoff.kora.* for any of them
Notes that @CassandraProfile is @Target(METHOD) and cannot be placed on the repository interface

evals.query: Model a Kora 2.0 Cassandra entity with a nested Address user-defined type (street, city, zipCode), plus a list of addresses and a set of tags of the same UDT.
expected_behavior: Annotates the Address type with @UDT from io.koraframework.database.cassandra.annotation and the owning DAO with @EntityCassandra
Maps the collection as List<Address> and notes that CQL needs LIST<FROZEN<address>>
States that only the scalar and List forms of a UDT get generated mappers, so Set<Address> (and Map<K, Address>) fail with 'No component found for dependency: CassandraRowColumnMapper<Set<Address>>'
Offers the two real options for the set: model the column as LIST<FROZEN<...>>, or hand-write a CassandraRowColumnMapper/CassandraParameterColumnMapper pair
Notes that @UDT takes no arguments and that the CQL type is resolved from the statement metadata by field name, not from the Java class name
Does not use JPA @Embeddable/@Embedded for the UDT

evals.query: Add a method that inserts many users in one batch, and another that loads users by a list of ids with an IN clause.
expected_behavior: Marks the list parameter with @Batch from io.koraframework.database.common.annotation and keeps a single-row INSERT bound to entity fields (:entity.id)
Returns void (or Unit, or CompletionStage<Void> in Java async) from the batch method, noting a batch produces no mapped result
Mentions that the generator builds a BatchStatement with DefaultBatchType.UNLOGGED and that batching across partitions is a Cassandra anti-pattern
For the IN clause, states that there is no built-in CassandraParameterColumnMapper<List<T>>, so a declarative :ids binding fails the graph
Uses executor() with CassandraQuery.named().bindIn("ids", ids) — which expands to one placeholder per element — or a hand-written list parameter mapper via @Mapping
Does not hand-build a BatchStatement in user code and does not use an external ORM

evals.query: I need an analytics query to run with ONE consistency and a 30s timeout while the rest of the repository stays on LOCAL_QUORUM.
expected_behavior: Defines cassandra.profiles.analytics overriding basic.request.consistency and basic.request.timeout with the full nested path
Sets the default cassandra.basic.request.consistency for everything else
Annotates the specific @Query method with @CassandraProfile("analytics") from io.koraframework.database.cassandra.annotation
Notes that @CassandraProfile is @Target(METHOD) and cannot be placed on the repository interface
Mentions that contactPoints cannot be overridden per profile and that unset profile keys fall back to the root section
Optionally offers CassandraQuery.opts(...) via executor() for one-off per-query tuning
Does not invent readConsistency/writeConsistency/retryPolicy keys or a JDBC-style @Transactional

evals.query: Add a conditional insert that only writes when the row does not already exist, and make the whole two-step write atomic.
expected_behavior: Writes CQL with IF NOT EXISTS in the @Query and returns boolean to read the [applied] flag, which is the first column of an LWT result
States that Cassandra has no transactions, that CassandraExecutor has no inTx, and that LWT is a single-partition compare-and-set rather than a multi-statement transaction
Declines to make the two-step write atomic across partitions and suggests reshaping the data model or accepting compensation instead
Mentions that LWT uses serial consistency configured at cassandra.basic.request.serialConsistency (SERIAL or LOCAL_SERIAL)
Notes the round-trip cost of LWT and warns against using it as the default write path
Does not present an UNLOGGED batch as a transaction

evals.query: Write a Kotlin Cassandra repository for Kora 2.0 with an entity, a custom enum column mapper for both directions, and CRUD methods.
expected_behavior: Applies the com.google.devtools.ksp plugin and uses ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors") — never annotationProcessor or kapt for the Kora processor
Pins Kotlin 2.4.20 with the KSP plugin 2.3.12 — the versions Kora 2.0.0.RC2 is built with
Declares @Repository interface extending CassandraRepository with plain fun methods returning T?, List<T> and Unit
Uses @field:Column / @field:Id on data class properties and plain Kotlin nullable types instead of any JSpecify annotation
Implements CassandraRowColumnMapper for reads and CassandraParameterColumnMapper for writes, declaring the write mapper's value parameter as T?
Applies both with repeated @Mapping annotations on the entity property
Leaves dependency-free non-open mappers without @Component, or explains why one is needed
Does not use suspend, Flow, Mono, Flux, Optional, or ru.tinkoff.kora imports
